Ishi, last member of the Yahi tribe. Spent years alone in the wilderness. In 1911, at around the age of 50, he walked out into the western world.

Widely acclaimed in his time as the "last wild Indian" in America, Ishi lived most of his life completely outside modern culture.

When asked his name, he said: "I have none, because there were no people to name me," meaning that no Yahi had ever spoken his name. He was taken in by anthropologists at the University of California, Berkeley, who both studied him and hired him as a research assistant. He lived most of his remaining five years in a university building (an apartment) in San Francisco.
